counterfactual_rationale: The record indicates fuse_allreduce_rms failed for the tp=1 edge case. A small configuration test including tensor-parallel size 1 would plausibly expose the incorrect fusion handling.
The QuickReduce inline asm used an instruction unsupported on CDNA and broke gfx942 builds. CDNA build CI over the all-reduce kernels would plausibly catch the assembler failure.

The GPU fault appears when a CP round-robin shard has exactly one row and retains an inflated stride. Edge tests with token counts equal to cp_size, especially under memcheck, would plausibly expose the bad row pitch.
The breakage is in trtllm-gen FP8 MoE backend selection and shared backend wiring. End-to-end DeepSeek FP8 or FP4 MoE accuracy tests with FlashInfer trtllm enabled would plausibly reveal it.

The CPU intel_amx speculative verify path used truncated sequence lengths and accepted tokens against a hole in context. A speculative-decoding parity or accuracy test on intel_amx would plausibly catch it.
The correction bias came from torch.empty and could be zero or NaN before initialization. An initcheck-style sanitizer or explicit uninitialized-memory check would plausibly flag the use.
The accuracy drop depends on Blackwell DeepGemm E8M0 scaling for Qwen3.5 FP8 and was measured in GSM8K CI. A Blackwell hardware accuracy matrix with the affected model would plausibly expose it.

The CUTLASS scaled-mm dispatch rejected particular per-token/per-channel scale group shapes on Hopper. Kernel-vs-reference tests varying transposed scale shapes would plausibly catch the unsupported-shape path.

The JIT RMSNorm kernel lacked implementations for small hidden sizes and a clean rejection for oversized 16384. Hidden-size edge tests over 64, 128, 256, and unsupported sizes would plausibly expose the compile failures.

The CUDA-graph padding path initialized req_to_token with torch.empty, allowing stale or out-of-bounds entries during capture. A sanitizer/initcheck run or graph-capture test with padded slots would plausibly detect the bad reads.

The record says FP8 MLA persistent metadata was computed unnecessarily for chunked prefills and mainly presents unit/benchmark validation. It does not establish incorrect output, crash, or availability failure from the extra computation.

Beyond log cleanup, the record fixes Dynamo graph breaks, CUDA-graph dedup registration, and decode-engine KV reservation. Compiled serving and CUDA-graph warmup tests would plausibly exercise these failures.
The FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE bug manifested as a model accuracy issue for TP=1 ModelOpt FP4/NVFP4 workloads. Real quantized-model evaluation distributions would plausibly reveal it.

The hang appears after an interrupted two-rank IPC JIT build leaves a stale lock. A cold-cache multi-rank warmup test with interrupted-build recovery or schedule perturbation would plausibly reproduce it.
The CPU attention refactor used BF16Vec16 and sysconf features unavailable on Apple Silicon M1. Building the CPU backend on older ARM/macOS in the hardware/compiler matrix would plausibly catch it.

The record frames the change as selecting FlashInfer fa2 instead of auto/fa3 for possible Hopper performance regressions, without establishing a concrete correctness, crash, or severe availability failure. It is coded as not confirmed kernel correctness.

The cudagraph page table was too narrow only when long speculative generations approached or exceeded the configured context length. Long-context edge tests near the req_to_token width would plausibly expose the shape mismatch.

The FlashInfer allreduce workspace was initialized in a compile pass skipped when a cached compiled module is loaded. A torch.compile/cache replay serving test would plausibly hit the uninitialized workspace path.

The assertion appears for models whose layers have differing attention hyperparameters before trtllm usage is known. Configuration-matrix tests over nonuniform window, soft-cap, and scale parameters would plausibly expose it.

The FA DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 path used prefix lengths where prefix-plus-extend cache extents were required, causing stale-memory reads and large reference differences. Draft-extend fixtures with varying prefix and extend lengths would plausibly catch it.

The CPU TP padding failed when padded heads did not make the FP8 weight partition divisible by the quantization block size. Shape tests crossing TP size and block-size divisibility would plausibly expose the ValueError.

The ROCm custom paged-attention backend crashed on encoder-decoder decode steps where key and value are None. An end-to-end Whisper or encoder-decoder test on ROCm custom paged attention would plausibly hit this path.
The TPU Pallas block-size choice led to incorrect VMEM estimation and potential OOM in TPU CI. TPU backend CI covering kv_cache_update block sizing would plausibly expose the failure.

The Aiter RMSNorm kernel faulted on strided higher-rank Q/K views that are valid PyTorch tensors but unsafe for the backend. Layout edge tests using non-contiguous 3D views on ROCm would plausibly reveal it.

The record has an empty motivation and only says to check AMD CI for an AMD RoPE definition change. It does not provide enough evidence to determine whether this fixed production kernel correctness or only build/registration details.

The crash requires mamba_cache_mode=all combined with speculative decoding, prefix caching, and CUDA-graph/eager variants. A full spec-decode prefix-cache matrix for hybrid Mamba models would plausibly expose it.

The FlashInfer kernel availability check could not be traced by torch.dynamo when serving a compiled FusedMoE model. A compiled serving startup test for the affected Qwen3-VL FP4 configuration would plausibly catch it.

The W8A8 kernel ran on Turing but then falsely raised a no-compiled-kernel error because of a missing early return. Turing hardware CI for INT8 W8A8 loading would plausibly expose the spurious failure.

The AMD HIP layernorm path called fused_add_rms_norm with the wrong signature, causing AMD CI failures. An AMD backend CI lane that exercises HIP layernorm would plausibly catch the argument mismatch.

The persistent top-k memset was conditional on a runtime threshold and therefore was not captured for CUDA graphs. A DeepSeek CUDA-graph serving test covering persistent top-k would plausibly reveal stale state.
